facts.statement: The genus Arctacanthus was described by Nielsen in 1932.
Dolophonodus is a synonym of the genus Arctacanthus.
Arctacanthus belongs to the parent group Hybodontiformes.
Arctacanthus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Arctacanthus lived during the Permian and possibly the Triassic periods.
facts.quote: Arctacanthus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish from the Permian and possibly Triassic periods.

facts.statement: Arctacanthus is known only from isolated hook-shaped ichthyoliths believed to be dermal denticles of a chimaeran.
facts.quote: They are known only by isolated hook-shaped "ichthyoliths" thought to represent dermal denticles of a chimaeran.

facts.statement: Some researchers have attributed the ichthyoliths of Arctacanthus to teeth or hybodont cephalic spines.
facts.quote: Some have attributed these to teeth or hybodont cephalic spines.

facts.statement: It is uncertain whether similar ichthyoliths found in Japan and China belong to the genus Arctacanthus due to differences in age, location, and size.
facts.quote: The large difference in age, location, and size means their attribution to this genus is uncertain
